question:
(a) Explain why the intensity of scattered electrons in the Davisson and Germer experiment varies with scattering angle.
(b) What conclusion was drawn from the agreement between the observed wavelength and de Broglie wavelength?

options.A:
(a) Scattered intensity is uniform because electrons are only particles.
(b) Agreement with de Broglie wavelength proved that electrons have no wave nature.
options.B:
(a) Electron waves scattered from different crystal planes interfere; constructive interference at certain angles gives maxima, so intensity varies with angle.
(b) Agreement between observed diffraction wavelength and $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{p}$ confirmed de Broglie matter waves and electron wave nature.
options.C:
(a) Intensity changes only because the electron charge changes with angle.
(b) The observed wavelength proved electrons are photons.
options.D:
(a) Crystal atoms absorb all electrons at certain angles.
(b) The agreement proved only the wave nature of nickel atoms.
